name: New Year's Eve
h1: New Year's Eve Charcuterie Board Ideas
seo_title: New Year's Eve Charcuterie Board Ideas: 9 Boards + a Midnight Plan
description: 9 New Year's Eve charcuterie board ideas: a Champagne board, caviar and chips, a luxury board, skewers, a whiskey and cheese board and a New Year's Day brunch board, plus a plan that lasts until midnight.
answer: It has to last until midnight, so plan about 3 oz each of cheese and meat per guest. Pour Champagne or Prosecco, and save half the food for a second round around 10 pm.

ideas.title: The Champagne Board
ideas.text: Built for bubbles: chunks of Parmigiano-Reggiano, a triple-crème, prosciutto, Marcona almonds, kettle chips, gougères and strawberries. Salt and fat are what make Champagne taste its best.

ideas.title: The Caviar and Chips Splurge
ideas.text: Kettle chips with crème fraîche and a tin of caviar or trout roe, blini, smoked salmon, chives and a good Comté, with a bottle of brut. Small portions, big effect.

ideas.title: The Midnight Refill Tray
ideas.text: Build one board for the start of the party and keep a second tray ready in the fridge: more cheese, salami, crackers and grapes, plus something warm like sliders for the 10 pm slump.

ideas.title: The New Year's Eve Board
ideas.text: The complete midnight board: sized as the party food, built to pair with sparkling wine, with a second round held back in the fridge.

ideas.title: The Luxury Board
ideas.text: Aged and rare cheeses, the best cured meats and a few luxury touches. For the night when one big board is the whole party.

ideas.title: The Cocktail Party Board
ideas.text: Everything is one or two bites, so guests can eat with a glass in hand. Salty, crisp and made to go with cocktails.

ideas.title: Charcuterie Skewers
ideas.text: Bites on sticks for a standing party: easy to make ahead, easy to refill and no crowd around one board.
ideas.on_it: Salami · mozzarella balls · tortellini · olives · cherry tomatoes · basil

ideas.title: The Whiskey and Cheese Board
ideas.link_text: Which cheeses go with which whiskey
ideas.text: Three or four cheeses matched to whiskey styles, with dark chocolate, nuts and dried fruit. A good fit for a quieter night in.
ideas.on_it: Aged cheddar · aged Gouda · blue cheese · dark chocolate · pecans · dried apricots

ideas.title: New Year's Day Bagel Board
ideas.text: Set it up the night before so brunch takes five minutes, whoever is hosting.
ideas.on_it: Bagels · cream cheeses · smoked salmon · capers · red onion · tomato · fruit

shapes.name: Midnight Clock Board
steps: On a round board, set a small bowl of jam or honey in the center.
Place 12 cheese cubes or cracker stacks around the edge as the hours.
Make the hands from two breadsticks or folded prosciutto, both pointing at 12.

shapes.name: Confetti Stripe Board
steps: On a rectangle, lay diagonal stripes of gold, white and dark: Gouda, Brie, salami, then repeat.
Fill the gaps between stripes with crackers and Marcona almonds.
Scatter pomegranate seeds or edible gold sprinkles over the top just before serving.

plan.what: Buy crackers, chips, nuts, jams and the sparkling wine.
Buy cheese, meat and fruit. Put the wine in the fridge.
Cut cheese, fold meats and pack the refill tray. Cover both and chill.
Take hard cheese out of the fridge and build the first board.
Swap in the refill tray. Anything perishable that has been out 2 hours goes back in the fridge or in the bin.

faq.q: What goes on a New Year's Eve charcuterie board?
faq.a: Salty, crisp and rich things that suit sparkling wine: Parmigiano-Reggiano, a triple-crème or Brie, prosciutto and salami, Marcona almonds, kettle chips, gougères and strawberries. Add one splurge, like smoked salmon or caviar, for midnight.

Salty, nutty and creamy cheeses: Parmigiano-Reggiano, aged Comté, Brie and triple-crème. The bubbles and acidity cut the fat, and the salt makes the wine taste fruitier. Strong blues tend to overpower a dry Champagne.

faq.q: How do I keep a charcuterie board fresh until midnight?
faq.a: Don't put everything out at once. Perishable food should sit out no more than 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F), so build a first board for the start of the party and keep a second tray in the fridge to swap in around 10 pm. Add crackers and chips last so they stay crisp.

faq.q: How much charcuterie do I need for a New Year's Eve party?
faq.a: If the board is the party food, plan about 3 oz each of cheese and meat per guest and 10 to 12 crackers; if there's dinner first, 2 oz of each is enough. From 20 guests, add 10%.

faq.q: What can I serve instead of expensive caviar?
faq.a: Trout or salmon roe gives the same salty pop for less. Serve it on kettle chips or blini with a spoon of crème fraîche or sour cream and chopped chives.

faq.q: How do you make a charcuterie board last until midnight?
faq.a: Put out half the food at the start and keep the rest covered in the fridge. Refill around 10 pm with fresh crackers and the second half of the cheese and meat.

faq.q: What are good New Year's Day brunch board ideas?
faq.a: A bagel board with cream cheeses, smoked salmon, capers, red onion and fruit. Set out everything but the fresh items the night before.

faq.q: How much does a New Year's Eve charcuterie board cost?
faq.a: As the party food, plan about $5 to $7 per guest on a budget and $8 to $12 for a standard board, so roughly $100 to $140 or $160 to $240 for 20 guests. Splurge cheeses and meats cost more. Store and region change the total.

mistakes.text: By 11 the board is picked over and warm. Put out half, keep half in the fridge and refill around 10.
Brie slumps over a long night. Lean on aged cheeses like Parmigiano, Comté and aged Gouda, which hold up.
The board is the party food, so plan about 3 oz each of cheese and meat per guest, not 2.
Put sparkling cider or a mocktail next to the Champagne so everyone has something to toast with.

ahead: 1 week: crackers, chips, nuts, jams and the sparkling wine
The morning of: cut cheese, fold meats and pack a second refill tray; cover both and chill
last: Build the first board in the last hour
Swap in the refill tray around 10 pm
Anything perishable out 2 hours goes back in the fridge or in the bin
